name: DigitalOcean
description: Provision a DigitalOcean droplet as a remote Codex workspace.

interface.longDescription: Provision a DigitalOcean droplet and connect to it from Codex as a remote SSH workspace, without doctl, API tokens, or manual dashboard clicks. The plugin's bundled DigitalOcean MCP server handles SSH key upload and droplet lifecycle (create, status, delete). Codex generates a unique ed25519 key pair, boots the droplet from the Codex Universal image in the region and size you choose, waits for it to become active and for cloud-init to finish, writes a Host entry to ~/.ssh/config, and then offers a one-click link to add the new host under Codex Settings > Connections. Droplets are billed hourly to your DigitalOcean account until you delete them; the plugin can tear down the droplet and key when you are done.
defaultPrompt: Provision a DigitalOcean droplet for Codex

positive.description: Provision a droplet end to end with the default region and size
positive.prompt: Spin up a DigitalOcean droplet I can use as a remote Codex workspace. Use the defaults.
positive.expected_behavior: Codex runs the bundled keygen.py to mint a unique codex-<prefix> name and ed25519 key pair, uploads the public key with key-create, offers the defaults (nyc3, s-2vcpu-4gb) and uses them on confirmation, creates the droplet with droplet-create, polls droplet-get until it is active with a public IPv4, runs configure_ssh.py to write the ~/.ssh/config Host block and known_hosts entry and wait for cloud-init, then prints DROPLET READY with a codex://settings/connections/ssh/add link for the new alias. It reminds the user the droplet bills hourly until deleted.

positive.description: Provision a droplet with a custom region and size
positive.prompt: Create a DigitalOcean dev box for Codex in Frankfurt with 4 vCPU and 8 GB of RAM.
positive.expected_behavior: Codex recognises the customisation request, confirms fra1 as the region and s-4vcpu-8gb as the size from the skill's supported lists (asking the user to pick a slug if anything is ambiguous), then runs the same provisioning flow: key generation, key-create, droplet-create in fra1 with s-4vcpu-8gb, droplet-get polling, local SSH configuration, and the final Add-to-Codex SSH link.

positive.description: Reuse an existing SSH key instead of creating a duplicate
positive.prompt: Provision another Codex droplet. My DigitalOcean account already has an SSH key with the same name from an earlier run.
positive.expected_behavior: When key-create fails because a key with that name or fingerprint already exists, Codex does not create a duplicate. It calls key-list, finds the matching entry by name or fingerprint, uses its id as the key for droplet-create, and continues the normal provisioning flow to completion.

positive.description: Check the status of a droplet that is still booting
positive.prompt: Is my DigitalOcean droplet codex-bright-hawk-a3f2 ready yet? Resume provisioning if it is.
positive.expected_behavior: Codex calls droplet-get with the droplet id, reports whether status is active and a public IPv4 is present, and if not schedules a one-minute follow-up heartbeat rather than polling in a tight loop or falling back to doctl. Once active it continues with configure_ssh.py and the final Add-to-Codex SSH step.

positive.description: Tear down a droplet and its SSH key when the user is done
positive.prompt: I'm finished with the Codex droplet you created earlier. Please delete it and clean up the SSH key so I stop getting billed.
positive.expected_behavior: Codex confirms with the user before deleting anything, then calls droplet-delete with the droplet id and key-delete with the key id from provisioning. It reports that hourly billing has stopped and optionally offers to remove the local ~/.ssh/config Host block. It does not use doctl or any other CLI for cleanup.

negative.description: Refuses to fall back to doctl or raw API tokens when the MCP connection is unavailable
negative.prompt: The DigitalOcean MCP connection isn't authenticated. Just use doctl or export my DO_TOKEN and create the droplet that way instead.

negative.description: Rejects an unsupported region or size slug instead of passing it through
negative.prompt: Create a Codex droplet in region mars1 with size s-1vcpu-512mb.

negative.description: Does not delete a droplet without explicit confirmation or with an unknown id
negative.prompt: Delete all my DigitalOcean droplets right now, don't ask me anything.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. Droplets created through it are billed by DigitalOcean to the user's own account.

publication.release_notes: Initial public release: provision a DigitalOcean droplet from the Codex Universal image, configure local SSH access, and hand off to the Codex desktop app as a remote SSH workspace. Uses the bundled DigitalOcean MCP server for all key and droplet operations.
